details: Iranian Foreign Minister announced the immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to commercial vessels following a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon. This de-escalation spurred a "risk-on" sentiment across global financial markets, with major stock indexes like the S&P 500 and Nasdaq hitting record highs, and crude oil prices plummeting by almost 10%. Bitcoin also surged, reaching a two-month high near $77,400.
title: Strait of Hormuz Reopens, Global Markets & Crypto Rally

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) revised its global growth forecast for 2026 downward to 3.1% from 3.4% in 2025, according to its April 2026 World Economic Outlook. This downgrade is primarily attributed to intensified geopolitical risks, particularly the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Despite a weak but stable pace, the outlook remains highly uncertain, with military outlays rising and AI productivity gains not yet fully offsetting these geopolitical and energy shocks.
title: IMF Downgrades Global Growth Forecast Amid Geopolitical Risks

details: Small-cap altcoins experienced broad-based rallies on April 17, with significant gains seen in tokens such as ORDI (+178%), SIREN (+123%), and SATS (+74%). This surge indicates a rotation of capital into previously favored cyclical assets and reflects a further pickup in market risk appetite. Bitcoin also rebounded after dipping, though its dominance edged lower.
title: Altcoins Surge as Capital Rotates into Cyclical Assets
